-- =============================================================
-- 13_fingrid_warehouse.sql
-- Raw Fingrid Open Data, one row per dataset and time slot, exactly as
-- the API publishes it (no resampling, no gap filling, no clamping).
--
--   fingrid_dataset      what each dataset is (filled by src/fingrid_catalog.py)
--   fingrid_observation  the values; loaded by src/sync_fingrid.py
--   forecast_vs_actual   Fingrid's own forecasts joined to what happened
--
-- Idempotent: safe to run on every setup.
-- =============================================================

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fingrid_dataset (
    dataset_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    key         VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    name        TEXT        NOT NULL,
    unit        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    kind        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
    resolution  INTERVAL    NOT NULL
);
-- (Re)defined separately so an existing table picks up new kinds.
ALTER TABLE fingrid_dataset DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS fingrid_dataset_kind_check;
ALTER TABLE fingrid_dataset ADD CONSTRAINT fingrid_dataset_kind_check
    CHECK (kind IN ('actual', 'forecast', 'capacity', 'balancing', 'emission', 'system', 'weather'));

-- Partitioned by month on start_time. Every query here filters one dataset and a
-- time range, so PostgreSQL reads only the months it needs (partition pruning) and,
-- inside each, the primary-key index (dataset_id, start_time).
-- benchmarks/index_benchmark.md measures the effect (scripts/benchmark_warehouse.py).
--
-- A database created before partitioning has a plain table: it is converted in
-- place (rows copied into monthly partitions). Views on the table are dropped first
-- and recreated below and in 14_co2_forecast.sql.
DO $$
BEGIN
    IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_class WHERE relname = 'fingrid_observation' AND relkind = 'r') THEN
        DROP VIEW IF EXISTS forecast_vs_actual;
        DROP VIEW IF EXISTS co2_hourly;
        ALTER TABLE fingrid_observation RENAME TO fingrid_observation_unpartitioned;
        ALTER TABLE fingrid_observation_unpartitioned RENAME CONSTRAINT fingrid_observation_pkey TO fingrid_observation_unpartitioned_pkey;
    END IF;
END $$;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fingrid_observation (
    dataset_id  INTEGER          NOT NULL REFERENCES fingrid_dataset (dataset_id),
    start_time  TIMESTAMPTZ      NOT NULL,
    end_time    TIMESTAMPTZ      NOT NULL,
    value       DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    fetched_at  TIMESTAMPTZ      NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (dataset_id, start_time),
    CONSTRAINT ck_fingrid_observation_slot CHECK (end_time > start_time)
) PARTITION BY RANGE (start_time);

-- Safety net for a row outside every monthly partition. It stays empty, because
-- the sync and the snapshot restore create the months they write first.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fingrid_observation_default PARTITION OF fingrid_observation DEFAULT;

-- Create the monthly partitions (UTC months) covering [first_day, last_day]; existing
-- ones are left alone. Returns how many were created.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION ensure_fingrid_partitions(first_day date, last_day date)
RETURNS int LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    m       date;
    created int := 0;
BEGIN
    FOR m IN SELECT generate_series(date_trunc('month', first_day), date_trunc('month', last_day),
                                    interval '1 month')::date
    LOOP
        IF to_regclass(format('fingrid_observation_%s', to_char(m, 'YYYY_MM'))) IS NULL THEN
            EXECUTE format('CREATE TABLE %I PARTITION OF fingrid_observation FOR VALUES FROM (%L) TO (%L)',
                           format('fingrid_observation_%s', to_char(m, 'YYYY_MM')),
                           (m::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'),
                           ((m + interval '1 month')::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'));
            created := created + 1;
        END IF;
    END LOOP;
    RETURN created;
END $$;

SELECT ensure_fingrid_partitions((now() - interval '450 days')::date, (now() + interval '60 days')::date);

DO $$
DECLARE lo date; hi date;
BEGIN
    IF to_regclass('fingrid_observation_unpartitioned') IS NOT NULL THEN
        SELECT min(start_time)::date, max(start_time)::date INTO lo, hi FROM fingrid_observation_unpartitioned;
        IF lo IS NOT NULL THEN
            PERFORM ensure_fingrid_partitions(lo, hi);
        END IF;
        INSERT INTO fingrid_observation SELECT * FROM fingrid_observation_unpartitioned;
        DROP TABLE fingrid_observation_unpartitioned;
    END IF;
END $$;

-- One row per 15-minute slot where both the actual value and a Fingrid forecast exist.
--   day_ahead: published once, the previous day at 12:00 Finnish time (datasets 246, 165)
--   intraday:  updated every 15 minutes; the stored value is the last update before
--              the slot (datasets 245, 166)
-- capacity_mw is the wind capacity Fingrid itself used for the forecast (dataset 268,
-- hourly), so wind errors can be expressed as a share of the fleet.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW forecast_vs_actual AS
WITH pairs (variable, product, actual_id, forecast_id) AS (
    VALUES ('wind',        'day_ahead', 75,  246),
           ('wind',        'intraday',  75,  245),
           ('consumption', 'day_ahead', 124, 165),
           ('consumption', 'intraday',  124, 166)
)
SELECT p.variable,
       p.product,
       a.start_time,
       a.value           AS actual_mw,
       f.value           AS forecast_mw,
       a.value - f.value AS error_mw,          -- positive: more than forecast
       c.value           AS capacity_mw        -- wind only, else NULL
FROM pairs p
JOIN fingrid_observation a
  ON a.dataset_id = p.actual_id
JOIN fingrid_observation f
  ON f.dataset_id = p.forecast_id
 AND f.start_time = a.start_time
LEFT JOIN fingrid_observation c
  ON p.variable = 'wind'
 AND c.dataset_id = 268
 AND c.start_time = date_trunc('hour', a.start_time);

-- 14_co2_forecast.sql
-- Forecast of the CO2 intensity of electricity consumed in Finland,
-- per hour of a Finnish calendar day. Fingrid publishes the intensity
-- only as it happens (dataset 396); this predicts it a day ahead.
--
-- Input: Fingrid's own day-ahead forecasts (published at 12:00 Finnish
-- time for the next day), combined into the residual load:
--     residual load = consumption (165) - wind (246) - solar (247)
-- Demand that wind and solar do not cover is met by imports and
-- thermal plants, so the intensity rises with it (r = 0.84 over the
-- last year).
--
-- Model, refitted for every target day D using only what was known
-- when D's forecast was made:
--   1. least-squares line  co2 = a + b * residual_load  over the 60
--      days that end two days before D (regr_intercept, regr_slope)
--   2. level correction: the line's mean error on day D-2, which
--      captures slow changes the residual load does not see (a nuclear
--      outage, import conditions)
--   3. floor: never below the lowest intensity seen in the training
--      window. On very windy days the line otherwise extrapolates below
--      anything ever measured (7% of hours; their error drops from
--      9.8 to 3.4 g). co2_unclamped keeps the line's own value, which
--      still orders the hours when several sit on the floor.
-- co2_naive is the baseline to beat: the same hour two days earlier.
--
-- Used by sql/analysis/18 (tomorrow) and 19 (backtest), so the live
-- forecast and its track record run the exact same SQL.
-- Techniques: views with FILTER aggregates, a set-returning SQL
--             function, regr_slope / regr_intercept, generate_series
-- =============================================================

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW co2_hourly AS
SELECT
    date_trunc('hour', start_time)                                         AS hour_start,
    (date_trunc('hour', start_time) AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki')::date  AS day_fi,
    CASE WHEN COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 396) = 4                 -- a complete hour only
         THEN AVG(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 396) END              AS co2_actual,
    AVG(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 165)
      - AVG(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 246)
      - COALESCE(AVG(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 247), 0)            AS residual_load_mw
FROM fingrid_observation
WHERE dataset_id IN (396, 165, 246, 247)
GROUP BY date_trunc('hour', start_time);


-- Dropped first: CREATE OR REPLACE cannot change the columns a function returns.
DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS co2_forecast(date, date, int);
CREATE FUNCTION co2_forecast(first_day date, last_day date, training_days int DEFAULT 60)
RETURNS TABLE (
    day_fi            date,
    hour_start        timestamptz,
    hour_fi           int,
    residual_load_mw  double precision,
    co2_forecast      double precision,
    co2_unclamped     double precision,
    co2_naive         double precision,
    co2_actual        double precision
)
LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
    WITH days AS (
        SELECT generate_series(first_day, last_day - 1, interval '1 day')::date AS d
    ),
    fit AS (
        SELECT days.d,
               regr_intercept(x.co2_actual, x.residual_load_mw) AS a,
               regr_slope(x.co2_actual, x.residual_load_mw)     AS b,
               MIN(x.co2_actual)                                AS floor_g
        FROM days
        JOIN co2_hourly x
          ON x.day_fi >= days.d - (training_days + 1)
         AND x.day_fi <  days.d - 1
        WHERE x.co2_actual IS NOT NULL AND x.residual_load_mw IS NOT NULL
        GROUP BY days.d
    ),
    level AS (
        SELECT f.d, AVG(x.co2_actual - (f.a + f.b * x.residual_load_mw)) AS correction
        FROM fit f
        JOIN co2_hourly x ON x.day_fi = f.d - 2
        WHERE x.co2_actual IS NOT NULL AND x.residual_load_mw IS NOT NULL
        GROUP BY f.d
    )
    SELECT f.d,
           t.hour_start,
           EXTRACT(HOUR FROM t.hour_start AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki')::int,
           t.residual_load_mw,
           GREATEST(f.a + f.b * t.residual_load_mw + COALESCE(l.correction, 0), f.floor_g),
           f.a + f.b * t.residual_load_mw + COALESCE(l.correction, 0),
           p.co2_actual,
           t.co2_actual
    FROM fit f
    JOIN co2_hourly t ON t.day_fi = f.d AND t.residual_load_mw IS NOT NULL
    LEFT JOIN level l ON l.d = f.d
    LEFT JOIN co2_hourly p ON p.hour_start = t.hour_start - interval '48 hours'
    WHERE f.b IS NOT NULL
$$;

-- 15_grid_events.sql
-- A log of unusual moments on the Finnish grid, from raw Fingrid data.
--
-- Four kinds of event, each with a threshold that is an operating
-- definition or stated relative to the data, not tuned by eye:
--   frequency_low / frequency_high
--       a 1-minute frequency sample (177) outside the Nordic normal
--       band 49.9-50.1 Hz; samples below 45 Hz are invalid (Fingrid
--       writes gaps as 0) and are skipped
--   nuclear_drop
--       Finnish nuclear output (188, 3-minute) at least 400 MW below
--       its highest value of the previous 15 minutes: a unit tripping
--       or being cut back fast
--   low_inertia
--       kinetic energy of the Nordic system (260) in the lowest 1% of
--       the requested window: little spinning mass to slow a frequency
--       fall, the situation fast reserves exist for
--   price_spike
--       imbalance price (319) of 1,000 EUR/MWh or more
--
-- Flagged samples of one kind are merged into a single event when the
-- gap between them is short (3 min for frequency, 30 min for nuclear,
-- none for the 15-minute series): the gaps-and-islands pattern.
--
-- For nuclear drops, freq_min_nearby is the lowest valid frequency
-- within 15 minutes of the event. It is a cross-check between two
-- independent sensors, and over the last year it shows that Finnish
-- nuclear drops rarely move the (Nordic-wide) frequency far: either
-- they were controlled ramps, or the brief nadir fell between the
-- 1-minute samples.
--
-- Techniques: set-returning SQL function, window frames with RANGE
--             intervals, gaps and islands (LAG + running SUM),
--             PERCENTILE_CONT, LATERAL subquery
-- =============================================================

DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS grid_events(timestamptz, timestamptz);
CREATE FUNCTION grid_events(from_ts timestamptz, to_ts timestamptz)
RETURNS TABLE (
    kind             text,
    start_time       timestamptz,
    end_time         timestamptz,
    peak             double precision,
    threshold        double precision,
    unit             text,
    samples          int,
    freq_min_nearby  double precision
)
LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
    WITH
    freq AS (
        SELECT start_time, end_time, value
        FROM fingrid_observation
        WHERE dataset_id = 177 AND value >= 45
          AND start_time >= from_ts AND start_time < to_ts
    ),
    nuclear AS (
        SELECT start_time, end_time,
               value - MAX(value) OVER (ORDER BY start_time
                                        RANGE BETWEEN interval '15 minutes' PRECEDING
                                                  AND interval '1 second' PRECEDING) AS drop_mw
        FROM fingrid_observation
        WHERE dataset_id = 188
          AND start_time >= from_ts - interval '15 minutes' AND start_time < to_ts
    ),
    inertia AS (
        SELECT start_time, end_time, value
        FROM fingrid_observation
        WHERE dataset_id = 260 AND start_time >= from_ts AND start_time < to_ts
    ),
    inertia_limit AS (
        SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(0.01) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY value) AS lim FROM inertia
    ),
    flagged AS (
        SELECT CASE WHEN value < 49.9 THEN 'frequency_low' ELSE 'frequency_high' END AS kind,
               start_time, end_time, value,
               CASE WHEN value < 49.9 THEN 49.9 ELSE 50.1 END AS threshold
        FROM freq WHERE value < 49.9 OR value > 50.1
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 'nuclear_drop', start_time, end_time, drop_mw, -400
        FROM nuclear WHERE drop_mw <= -400 AND start_time >= from_ts
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 'low_inertia', i.start_time, i.end_time, i.value, l.lim
        FROM inertia i CROSS JOIN inertia_limit l WHERE i.value < l.lim
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 'price_spike', start_time, end_time, value, 1000
        FROM fingrid_observation
        WHERE dataset_id = 319 AND value >= 1000
          AND start_time >= from_ts AND start_time < to_ts
    ),
    starts AS (
        SELECT flagged.*,
               CASE WHEN start_time - LAG(end_time) OVER (PARTITION BY kind ORDER BY start_time)
                         <= CASE kind WHEN 'nuclear_drop' THEN interval '30 minutes'
                                      WHEN 'frequency_low' THEN interval '3 minutes'
                                      WHEN 'frequency_high' THEN interval '3 minutes'
                                      ELSE interval '0' END
                    THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS is_new
        FROM flagged
    ),
    islands AS (
        SELECT starts.*, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY kind ORDER BY start_time) AS event_no
        FROM starts
    ),
    events AS (
        SELECT kind,
               MIN(start_time) AS start_time,
               MAX(end_time)   AS end_time,
               CASE WHEN kind IN ('frequency_high', 'price_spike') THEN MAX(value) ELSE MIN(value) END AS peak,
               MIN(threshold)  AS threshold,
               COUNT(*)::int   AS samples
        FROM islands
        GROUP BY kind, event_no
    )
    SELECT e.kind, e.start_time, e.end_time, e.peak, e.threshold,
           CASE e.kind WHEN 'nuclear_drop' THEN 'MW' WHEN 'low_inertia' THEN 'GWs'
                       WHEN 'price_spike' THEN 'EUR/MWh' ELSE 'Hz' END,
           e.samples,
           f.freq_min
    FROM events e
    LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT MIN(x.value) AS freq_min
        FROM fingrid_observation x
        WHERE e.kind = 'nuclear_drop'
          AND x.dataset_id = 177 AND x.value >= 45
          AND x.start_time BETWEEN e.start_time - interval '15 minutes' AND e.end_time + interval '15 minutes'
    ) f ON true
$$;

-- 13_forecast_scorecard.sql
-- How far were Fingrid's own forecasts from what actually happened?
--
-- One row per variable (wind, consumption) and forecast product:
--   day_ahead  published the previous day at 12:00 Finnish time
--   intraday   updated every 15 minutes (last update before the slot)
--
--   mae_mw               mean absolute error per 15-minute slot
--   bias_mw              mean error; positive = reality above forecast
--   rmse_mw              punishes large misses more than MAE
--   p95_abs_error_mw     95 in 100 slots missed by less than this
--   wape_pct             total absolute error / total actual, in percent
--   mae_pct_of_capacity  wind only: MAE as a share of the wind fleet
--                        that Fingrid assumed (dataset 268)
--
-- Parameters: start, end (timestamptz, end exclusive)
-- Techniques: views, ordered-set aggregates (PERCENTILE_CONT), NULLIF
-- =============================================================

SELECT
    variable,
    product,
    COUNT(*)                                                     AS slots,
    AVG(ABS(error_mw))                                           AS mae_mw,
    AVG(error_mw)                                                AS bias_mw,
    SQRT(AVG(error_mw * error_mw))                               AS rmse_mw,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ABS(error_mw))  AS p95_abs_error_mw,
    100 * SUM(ABS(error_mw)) / NULLIF(SUM(actual_mw), 0)         AS wape_pct,
    100 * AVG(ABS(error_mw)) / NULLIF(AVG(capacity_mw), 0)       AS mae_pct_of_capacity,
    AVG(actual_mw)                                               AS mean_actual_mw,
    AVG(capacity_mw)                                             AS mean_capacity_mw
FROM forecast_vs_actual
WHERE start_time >= %(start)s
  AND start_time <  %(end)s
GROUP BY variable, product
ORDER BY variable, product;

-- =============================================================
-- 17_forecast_error_vs_balancing.sql
-- What happens on the grid when the day-ahead forecasts are wrong?
--
-- net_surprise_mw = wind error - consumption error (day-ahead):
--   negative: less wind and/or more demand than forecast (system short)
--   positive: more wind and/or less demand than forecast (system long)
-- Slots are grouped in 500 MW bins (open-ended below -1500 and from
-- +1500 up). Each bin shows averages of:
--   mfrr_need   Fingrid's estimate of the mFRR energy needed (377)
--   mfrr_up     activated upward mFRR, published as values >= 0 (375)
--   mfrr_down   activated downward mFRR, published as values <= 0 (376)
-- and the median imbalance price (319). Net activation is up + down.
--
-- This is an association, not a cause: market parties trade after the
-- day-ahead forecast, and many other things move the balance.
--
-- Parameters: start, end (timestamptz, end exclusive)
-- Techniques: self-join of a view, LEFT JOINs, FLOOR binning with
--             LEAST/GREATEST, PERCENTILE_CONT, corr() aggregate
-- =============================================================

WITH surprise AS (
    SELECT w.start_time,
           w.error_mw - c.error_mw AS net_surprise_mw
    FROM forecast_vs_actual w
    JOIN forecast_vs_actual c
      ON c.start_time = w.start_time
     AND c.variable = 'consumption'
     AND c.product  = 'day_ahead'
     -- implied by the join, but PostgreSQL does not carry a range across it: without this
     -- line the consumption side reads the whole history, not just the window
     AND c.start_time >= %(start)s
     AND c.start_time <  %(end)s
    WHERE w.variable = 'wind'
      AND w.product  = 'day_ahead'
      AND w.start_time >= %(start)s
      AND w.start_time <  %(end)s
),
joined AS (
    SELECT s.start_time,
           s.net_surprise_mw,
           nd.value  AS mfrr_need_mw,
           up.value  AS mfrr_up_mw,
           dn.value  AS mfrr_down_mw,
           px.value  AS imbalance_price
    FROM surprise s
    LEFT JOIN fingrid_observation nd ON nd.dataset_id = 377 AND nd.start_time = s.start_time
    LEFT JOIN fingrid_observation up ON up.dataset_id = 375 AND up.start_time = s.start_time
    LEFT JOIN fingrid_observation dn ON dn.dataset_id = 376 AND dn.start_time = s.start_time
    LEFT JOIN fingrid_observation px ON px.dataset_id = 319 AND px.start_time = s.start_time
),
binned AS (
    SELECT joined.*,
           LEAST(GREATEST(FLOOR(net_surprise_mw / 500) * 500, -2000), 1500) AS bin
    FROM joined
)
SELECT
    CASE WHEN bin = -2000 THEN NULL ELSE bin END        AS bin_from_mw,
    CASE WHEN bin =  1500 THEN NULL ELSE bin + 500 END  AS bin_to_mw,
    COUNT(*)                                            AS slots,
    AVG(net_surprise_mw)                                AS mean_net_surprise_mw,
    AVG(mfrr_need_mw)                                   AS mean_mfrr_need_mw,
    AVG(mfrr_up_mw)                                     AS mean_mfrr_up_mw,
    AVG(mfrr_down_mw)                                   AS mean_mfrr_down_mw,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY imbalance_price) AS median_imbalance_price,
    AVG(imbalance_price)                                AS mean_imbalance_price,
    (SELECT corr(net_surprise_mw, mfrr_need_mw) FROM joined)              AS r_surprise_vs_mfrr_need,
    (SELECT corr(net_surprise_mw, mfrr_up_mw + mfrr_down_mw) FROM joined) AS r_surprise_vs_net_mfrr,
    (SELECT corr(net_surprise_mw, imbalance_price) FROM joined)           AS r_surprise_vs_price
FROM binned
GROUP BY bin
ORDER BY bin;

-- =============================================================
-- 23_temperature_sensitivity.sql
-- How much does each degree of cold raise Finland's electricity use?
--
-- A "hinge" model per day type (weekday / weekend):
--     consumption = base_mw + mw_per_degree * max(balance_point - temp, 0)
-- Above the balance point consumption barely depends on temperature;
-- below it, heating adds a roughly fixed amount per degree. The balance
-- point is not chosen by hand: the line is fitted for every whole degree
-- from 5 to 20 °C and the one with the highest r² is kept.
--
--   mw_per_degree   extra average load for each degree below the
--                   balance point
--   pct_per_degree  the same as a share of the mean consumption
--   base_mw         consumption at or above the balance point
--
-- Parameters: start, end (timestamptz, end exclusive)
-- Techniques: generate_series as a parameter grid, regr_slope /
--             regr_intercept / regr_r2, DISTINCT ON to pick the best fit
-- =============================================================

WITH city_days AS (
    SELECT dataset_id, (start_time AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki')::date AS day_fi, AVG(value) AS temp_c
    FROM fingrid_observation
    WHERE dataset_id IN (178, 182, 196, 185)
      AND start_time >= %(start)s AND start_time < %(end)s
    GROUP BY dataset_id, day_fi
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 400
),
days AS (
    SELECT t.day_fi, t.temp_c, c.consumption_mw,
           CASE WHEN EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM t.day_fi) >= 6 THEN 'weekend' ELSE 'weekday' END AS day_type
    FROM (SELECT day_fi, AVG(temp_c) AS temp_c FROM city_days GROUP BY day_fi HAVING COUNT(*) = 4) t
    JOIN (SELECT (start_time AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki')::date AS day_fi, AVG(value) AS consumption_mw
          FROM fingrid_observation
          WHERE dataset_id = 124 AND start_time >= %(start)s AND start_time < %(end)s
          GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(*) >= 92) c USING (day_fi)
),
fits AS (
    SELECT day_type,
           bp                                                        AS balance_point_c,
           regr_slope(consumption_mw, GREATEST(bp - temp_c, 0))      AS mw_per_degree,
           regr_intercept(consumption_mw, GREATEST(bp - temp_c, 0))  AS base_mw,
           regr_r2(consumption_mw, GREATEST(bp - temp_c, 0))         AS r2,
           COUNT(*)                                                  AS days,
           AVG(consumption_mw)                                       AS mean_consumption_mw,
           MIN(temp_c)                                               AS coldest_c,
           MAX(temp_c)                                               AS warmest_c
    FROM days CROSS JOIN generate_series(5, 20) AS bp
    GROUP BY day_type, bp
)
SELECT DISTINCT ON (day_type)
       day_type, balance_point_c, mw_per_degree,
       100 * mw_per_degree / mean_consumption_mw AS pct_per_degree,
       base_mw, r2, days, mean_consumption_mw, coldest_c, warmest_c
FROM fits
WHERE mw_per_degree IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY day_type, r2 DESC;

-- =============================================================
-- 24_wind_allocation_panel.sql
-- One row per UTC hour: Finland's power balance split into its
-- parts, the input of the "where does an extra MW of wind go?"
-- regression in src/wind_allocation.py.
--
--   consumption_mw   dataset 124, 4 quarters per hour
--   wind_mw          dataset 75, 4 quarters
--   nuclear_mw       dataset 188, 3-minute readings (>= 16 of 20)
--   hydro_mw         dataset 191, 3-minute readings (>= 16 of 20)
--   other_mw         production (74) - wind - nuclear - hydro:
--                    CHP, condensing power, solar, batteries, ...
--   net_import_mw    consumption - production, which is how Fingrid
--                    defines consumption (124 = production + import
--                    - export)
--   net_import_measured_mw
--                    -1 x dataset 194, the measured net export, as an
--                    independent check of net_import_mw
--   battery_mw       dataset 398, battery discharge (>= 16 of 20)
--   import_sweden_north_mw, import_sweden_central_mw,
--   import_estonia_mw, import_norway_mw
--                    -1 x the measured flow on each border (60, 61, 55,
--                    57; positive = import, 4 quarters per hour); NULL
--                    unless all four borders are complete
--   import_unmeasured_mw
--                    net_import_mw - the four borders: Åland, metering
--                    and timing differences
--   chp_district_heating_mw, chp_industrial_mw, reserve_and_small_mw
--                    datasets 201, 202, 205 (>= 16 of 20 each); NULL
--                    unless all three are complete
--   other_rest_mw    other_mw - the three: condensing power, solar, ...
--   temp_c           mean of Helsinki, Jyväskylä, Oulu, Rovaniemi

-- By construction consumption = wind + nuclear + hydro + other
-- + net_import, so the four responses to +1 MW of wind add up to
-- 1 MW: whatever wind does not push out of imports, hydro or other
-- production must show up as extra consumption. The border and plant
-- columns split imports and other production further, and add up to
-- them exactly (the remainder columns close the gap).
--
-- Parameters: start, end (timestamptz, end exclusive)
-- Techniques: FILTER pivot, HAVING completeness rules, AT TIME ZONE
-- =============================================================

WITH hourly AS (
    SELECT dataset_id,
           date_trunc('hour', start_time) AS hour_start,
           AVG(value)                     AS value,
           COUNT(*)                       AS n
    FROM fingrid_observation
    WHERE dataset_id IN (74, 75, 124, 188, 191, 194, 398, 178, 182, 196, 185,
                         55, 57, 60, 61, 201, 202, 205)
      AND start_time >= %(start)s AND start_time < %(end)s
    GROUP BY dataset_id, hour_start
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= CASE WHEN dataset_id IN (74, 75, 124, 55, 57, 60, 61) THEN 4 ELSE 16 END
),
wide AS (
    SELECT hour_start,
           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 124) AS consumption_mw,
           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 74)  AS production_mw,
           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 75)  AS wind_mw,
           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 188) AS nuclear_mw,
           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 191) AS hydro_mw,
           -MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 194) AS net_import_measured_mw,
           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 398) AS battery_mw,
           -MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 60) AS import_sweden_north_mw,
           -MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 61) AS import_sweden_central_mw,
           -MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 55) AS import_estonia_mw,
           -MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 57) AS import_norway_mw,
           COUNT(*)   FILTER (WHERE dataset_id IN (55, 57, 60, 61)) AS borders,
           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 201) AS chp_district_heating_mw,
           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 202) AS chp_industrial_mw,
           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 205) AS reserve_and_small_mw,
           COUNT(*)   FILTER (WHERE dataset_id IN (201, 202, 205)) AS plants,
           AVG(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id IN (178, 182, 196, 185)) AS temp_c,
           COUNT(*)   FILTER (WHERE dataset_id IN (178, 182, 196, 185)) AS cities
    FROM hourly
    GROUP BY hour_start
)
SELECT hour_start,
       EXTRACT(HOUR   FROM hour_start AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki')::int AS hour_fi,
       EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM hour_start AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki')::int AS isodow_fi,
       EXTRACT(MONTH  FROM hour_start AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki')::int AS month_fi,
       consumption_mw,
       wind_mw,
       nuclear_mw,
       hydro_mw,
       production_mw - wind_mw - nuclear_mw - hydro_mw AS other_mw,
       consumption_mw - production_mw                  AS net_import_mw,
       net_import_measured_mw,
       battery_mw,
       temp_c,
       CASE WHEN borders = 4 THEN import_sweden_north_mw END   AS import_sweden_north_mw,
       CASE WHEN borders = 4 THEN import_sweden_central_mw END AS import_sweden_central_mw,
       CASE WHEN borders = 4 THEN import_estonia_mw END        AS import_estonia_mw,
       CASE WHEN borders = 4 THEN import_norway_mw END         AS import_norway_mw,
       CASE WHEN borders = 4 THEN consumption_mw - production_mw - import_sweden_north_mw
            - import_sweden_central_mw - import_estonia_mw - import_norway_mw END AS import_unmeasured_mw,

  AND wind_mw IS NOT NULL AND nuclear_mw IS NOT NULL AND hydro_mw IS NOT NULL
  AND cities = 4

"""
wind_allocation.py
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Where does an extra MW of wind go? And an extra MW of nuclear?

Fingrid defines consumption as production + import - export, so every hour

    consumption = wind + nuclear + hydro + other + net_import

(sql/analysis/24_wind_allocation_panel.sql builds that hourly table). Each
part except wind and nuclear is regressed on

    wind, nuclear, heating = max(15 C - temperature, 0)
    + fixed effects for the Finnish hour of day, weekday and month

and the wind coefficients of net_import, hydro and other say how much of an
extra MW of wind pushes out imports, hydro and other production. Because of
the identity, 1 - (those three) is the extra consumption that goes with it;
it is also estimated directly, and the two agree to rounding.

Hourly power data is autocorrelated, so the 95 % intervals use Newey-West
(HAC) standard errors with a Bartlett kernel over 24 hourly lags; plain OLS
intervals would be several times too narrow.

breakdown() then asks which border the lower imports come from and which
plants make room: the same regression on each border's measured import and on
each kind of plant, fitted on the hours where all of them are known. OLS is
linear in the response, so the border shares add up to the import share and
the plant shares to the other-production share of those same hours exactly.

These are associations after controlling for weather and the calendar, not
proven causal effects: wind is close to exogenous (the weather decides it),
nuclear output less so (outages are planned around demand and prices).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

HEATING_BALANCE_C = 15.0        # from the weekday fit in sql/analysis/23_temperature_sensitivity.sql
HAC_LAGS = 24
DRIVERS = ("wind_mw", "nuclear_mw")
RESPONSES = ("net_import_mw", "hydro_mw", "other_mw", "consumption_mw")
BORDERS = ("import_sweden_north_mw", "import_sweden_central_mw", "import_estonia_mw", "import_norway_mw",
           "import_unmeasured_mw")
PLANTS = ("chp_district_heating_mw", "chp_industrial_mw", "reserve_and_small_mw", "other_rest_mw")
SEASONS = {"winter": (12, 1, 2), "spring": (3, 4, 5), "summer": (6, 7, 8), "autumn": (9, 10, 11)}
Z95 = 1.959964


def _column(rows: list[dict], key: str) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.array([np.nan if r[key] is None else float(r[key]) for r in rows])


def _dummies(values: np.ndarray) -> list[np.ndarray]:
    """One column per level except the first (the constant absorbs it)."""
    levels = sorted(set(values.tolist()))
    return [(values == v).astype(float) for v in levels[1:]]


def design(rows: list[dict]) -> tuple[np.ndarray, list[str]]:
    """Regressors: constant, wind, nuclear, heating, then hour/weekday/month dummies."""
    heating = np.maximum(HEATING_BALANCE_C - _column(rows, "temp_c"), 0.0)
    cols = [np.ones(len(rows)), _column(rows, "wind_mw"), _column(rows, "nuclear_mw"), heating]
    names = ["const", "wind_mw", "nuclear_mw", "heating_degc"]
    for key in ("hour_fi", "isodow_fi", "month_fi"):
        dummies = _dummies(np.array([r[key] for r in rows]))
        cols += dummies
        names += [f"{key}_{i}" for i in range(len(dummies))]
    return np.column_stack(cols), names


def newey_west(X: np.ndarray, resid: np.ndarray, lags: int = HAC_LAGS) -> np.ndarray:
    """HAC covariance of the OLS coefficients (Bartlett kernel)."""
    Z = X * resid[:, None]
    S = Z.T @ Z
    for lag in range(1, lags + 1):
        w = 1.0 - lag / (lags + 1.0)
        G = Z[lag:].T @ Z[:-lag]
        S += w * (G + G.T)
    XtX_inv = np.linalg.inv(X.T @ X)
    return XtX_inv @ S @ XtX_inv


def fit(rows: list[dict], responses=RESPONSES) -> dict:
    """OLS with HAC intervals for each response; rows with any missing value are dropped."""
    X, names = design(rows)
    out = {"hours": 0, "responses": {}}
    for response in responses:
        y = _column(rows, response)
        keep = ~np.isnan(y) & ~np.isnan(X).any(axis=1)
        Xk, yk = X[keep], y[keep]
        beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(Xk, yk, rcond=None)
        resid = yk - Xk @ beta
        se = np.sqrt(np.diag(newey_west(Xk, resid)))
        r2 = 1.0 - resid.var() / yk.var()
        coefs = {}
        for driver in DRIVERS:
            i = names.index(driver)
            coefs[driver] = {"coef": float(beta[i]), "se": float(se[i]),
                             "ci_low": float(beta[i] - Z95 * se[i]), "ci_high": float(beta[i] + Z95 * se[i])}
        out["responses"][response] = {"r2": float(r2), "hours": int(keep.sum()), **coefs}
        out["hours"] = max(out["hours"], int(keep.sum()))
    return out


def split(fitted: dict, driver: str) -> dict:
    """Shares of +1 MW of *driver*: pushed out of imports, hydro and other production, and the rest.
    The rest equals the directly estimated consumption response up to rounding (the identity)."""
    r = fitted["responses"]
    pushed = {k: -r[k][driver]["coef"] for k in ("net_import_mw", "hydro_mw", "other_mw")}
    return {**pushed, "consumption_rest": 1.0 - sum(pushed.values()),
            "consumption_direct": r["consumption_mw"][driver]["coef"]}


def by_season(rows: list[dict]) -> dict:
    out = {}
    for season, months in SEASONS.items():
        part = [r for r in rows if r["month_fi"] in months]
        if len(part) >= 24 * 30:
            out[season] = fit(part)
    return out


def breakdown(rows: list[dict], min_hours: int = 24 * 300) -> dict | None:
    """Wind and nuclear coefficients of every border and plant column, plus their parents
    (net_import_mw, other_mw), on the hours where all of them are present."""
    part = [r for r in rows if all(r.get(k) is not None for k in BORDERS + PLANTS)]
    if len(part) < min_hours:
        return None
    return fit(part, ("net_import_mw", "other_mw") + BORDERS + PLANTS)

-- the input of the uncertainty ranges in src/forecast_ranges.py.
--
--   variable      'wind'        day-ahead forecast 246, actual 75
--                 'consumption' day-ahead forecast 165, actual 124
--   forecast_mw   mean of the four quarter-hour forecasts
--   actual_mw     mean of the four measured quarters; NULL for hours

-- (fingrid_catalog.STORE_FUTURE), so every row is the forecast as

WITH hourly AS (
    SELECT dataset_id,
           date_trunc('hour', start_time) AS hour_start,

    FROM fingrid_observation
    WHERE dataset_id IN (75, 124, 165, 246)
      AND start_time >= %(start)s AND start_time < %(end)s
    GROUP BY dataset_id, hour_start
    HAVING COUNT(*) = 4
),
pairs AS (
    SELECT f.hour_start, v.variable, f.value AS forecast_mw, a.value AS actual_mw
    FROM (VALUES ('wind', 246, 75), ('consumption', 165, 124)) AS v (variable, forecast_id, actual_id)
    JOIN hourly f ON f.dataset_id = v.forecast_id

       actual_mw
FROM pairs
ORDER BY variable, hour_start;

"""
forecast_ranges.py
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
How wrong will tomorrow's forecast be? Calibrated ranges around Fingrid's
day-ahead wind and consumption forecasts.

Fingrid publishes one number per quarter-hour for tomorrow. Its own history of
errors (sql/analysis/25_forecast_errors_hourly.sql) says how far reality tends
to land from that number, and conformal prediction turns that history into
80 % and 95 % ranges with a coverage guarantee: if the coming errors behave
like the recent ones, at least that share of hours falls inside.

Methods, from simplest to the one published:

  global     split conformal on all recent errors
             (quantiles with the finite-sample correction ceil((n+1)(1-a))/n)
  by_hour    the same per block of six Finnish hours
  mondrian   per (six-hour block x forecast-level tercile): the error of a
             high wind forecast is several times that of a low one
  adaptive   mondrian with adaptive conformal inference (Gibbs & Candès 2021):
             after each day the miss rate a_t moves by gamma * (a - misses),
             so the ranges widen after a run of misses and narrow again
             when the forecast settles  -> published

Honest by construction: a day D is forecast from the errors of the CAL_DAYS
days that ended two days before it (day D-1 is still running when Fingrid
issues the forecast for D at 12:00 Finnish time), and the backtest replays
exactly that, day by day.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date, timedelta

import numpy as np

CAL_DAYS = 90            # errors used to calibrate each day's ranges
MIN_CAL_DAYS = 60        # fewer known days than this: no range
LEVELS = (0.80, 0.95)
GAMMA = 0.05             # ACI step per day
ALPHA_FLOOR = 0.25       # ACI may tighten the miss rate to at most a quarter of the nominal one
METHODS = ("global", "by_hour", "mondrian", "adaptive")
PUBLISHED = "adaptive"
HOUR_BLOCKS = 4          # 00-05, 06-11, 12-17, 18-23 Finnish time


def conformal_interval(residuals: np.ndarray, alpha: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Lower and upper residual bounds that cover >= 1 - alpha of exchangeable new residuals."""
    r = np.sort(residuals)
    n = len(r)
    if n == 0:
        return -math.inf, math.inf
    lo_rank = math.floor((n + 1) * alpha / 2)              # 1-based order statistics
    hi_rank = math.ceil((n + 1) * (1 - alpha / 2))
    lo = r[lo_rank - 1] if lo_rank >= 1 else -math.inf
    hi = r[hi_rank - 1] if hi_rank <= n else math.inf
    return float(lo), float(hi)


class Series:
    """One variable's hourly forecast/actual history, indexed by Finnish day."""

    def __init__(self, rows: list[dict]):
        rows = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r["hour_start"])
        as_date = lambda d: date.fromisoformat(d[:10]) if isinstance(d, str) else d
        self.day = np.array([as_date(r["day_fi"]) for r in rows])
        self.hour = np.array([r["hour_fi"] for r in rows])
        self.forecast = np.array([float(r["forecast_mw"]) for r in rows])
        self.actual = np.array([np.nan if r["actual_mw"] is None else float(r["actual_mw"]) for r in rows])
        self.residual = self.actual - self.forecast
        self.by_day = defaultdict(list)
        for i, d in enumerate(self.day):
            self.by_day[d].append(i)

    def calibration(self, target: date) -> np.ndarray:
        """Indices of known errors in the CAL_DAYS days ending two days before *target*."""
        last = target - timedelta(days=2)
        idx = [i for k in range(CAL_DAYS) for i in self.by_day.get(last - timedelta(days=k), [])]
        idx = np.array(idx, dtype=int)
        return idx[~np.isnan(self.residual[idx])] if len(idx) else idx

    def known_days(self, idx: np.ndarray) -> int:
        return len(set(self.day[idx].tolist()))


def _groups(s: Series, idx: np.ndarray, target_idx: np.ndarray, method: str):
    """Group label of each calibration row and each target row."""
    if method == "global":
        return np.zeros(len(idx), int), np.zeros(len(target_idx), int)
    block = lambda h: h * HOUR_BLOCKS // 24
    if method == "by_hour":
        return block(s.hour[idx]), block(s.hour[target_idx])
    cuts = np.quantile(s.forecast[idx], [1 / 3, 2 / 3])            # level terciles of the calibration window
    level = lambda f: np.searchsorted(cuts, f)
    return (block(s.hour[idx]) * 3 + level(s.forecast[idx]),
            block(s.hour[target_idx]) * 3 + level(s.forecast[target_idx]))


def ranges_for_day(s: Series, target: date, method: str, alphas: dict) -> dict | None:
    """{level: (lo, hi) arrays} for the hours of *target*, or None without enough history."""
    idx = s.calibration(target)
    tgt = np.array(s.by_day.get(target, []), dtype=int)
    if len(tgt) == 0 or s.known_days(idx) < MIN_CAL_DAYS:
        return None
    g_cal, g_tgt = _groups(s, idx, tgt, "mondrian" if method == "adaptive" else method)
    out = {}
    for level in LEVELS:
        alpha = alphas[level] if method == "adaptive" else 1 - level
        lo, hi = np.empty(len(tgt)), np.empty(len(tgt))
        for g in set(g_tgt.tolist()):
            ql, qh = conformal_interval(s.residual[idx][g_cal == g], alpha)
            if not (math.isfinite(ql) and math.isfinite(qh)):        # group too small for this level:
                ql, qh = conformal_interval(s.residual[idx], alpha)  # use every error in the window
            lo[g_tgt == g], hi[g_tgt == g] = ql, qh
        out[level] = (s.forecast[tgt] + lo, s.forecast[tgt] + hi)
    return {"idx": tgt, "bounds": out}


def _step(alpha: float, level: float, miss: float) -> float:
    """One ACI update: more misses than 1 - level lower alpha (wider ranges), fewer raise it."""
    return float(min(max(alpha + GAMMA * ((1 - level) - miss), ALPHA_FLOOR * (1 - level)), 0.5))


def interval_score(y, lo, hi, alpha) -> np.ndarray:
    """Winkler / interval score: width plus 2/alpha times the miss distance (lower is better)."""
    return (hi - lo) + (2 / alpha) * np.maximum(lo - y, 0) + (2 / alpha) * np.maximum(y - hi, 0)


def clip(variable: str, a: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    return np.maximum(a, 0.0) if variable == "wind" else a        # wind output cannot go below zero


def backtest(s: Series, variable: str, days: list[date]) -> dict:
    """Replay every day in *days*: ranges from what was known then, scored on what happened.
    Returns per-method scores, the adaptive alphas reached, and the per-day ranges of the published method."""
    alphas = {lv: 1 - lv for lv in LEVELS}
    scores = {m: {lv: {"hits": 0, "n": 0, "width": 0.0, "score": 0.0} for lv in LEVELS} for m in METHODS}
    published, pending = {}, []                  # ACI updates wait until their day is known at issue time
    for d in days:
        while pending and pending[0][0] <= d - timedelta(days=2):
            _, misses = pending.pop(0)
            for lv, miss in misses.items():
                alphas[lv] = _step(alphas[lv], lv, miss)
        for m in METHODS:
            r = ranges_for_day(s, d, m, alphas)
            if r is None:
                continue
            y = s.actual[r["idx"]]
            ok = ~np.isnan(y)
            for lv in LEVELS:
                lo, hi = (clip(variable, b) for b in r["bounds"][lv])
                inside = (y[ok] >= lo[ok]) & (y[ok] <= hi[ok])
                sc = scores[m][lv]
                sc["hits"] += int(inside.sum()); sc["n"] += int(ok.sum())
                sc["width"] += float((hi[ok] - lo[ok]).sum())
                sc["score"] += float(interval_score(y[ok], lo[ok], hi[ok], 1 - lv).sum())
            if m == PUBLISHED:
                published[d] = r
                if ok.any():
                    misses = {}
                    for lv in LEVELS:
                        lo, hi = (clip(variable, b) for b in r["bounds"][lv])
                        misses[lv] = float(1 - ((y[ok] >= lo[ok]) & (y[ok] <= hi[ok])).mean())
                    pending.append((d, misses))
    for day, misses in pending:                  # days known by now count for tomorrow's alphas
        for lv, miss in misses.items():
            alphas[lv] = _step(alphas[lv], lv, miss)
    table = {m: {lv: {"coverage": v["hits"] / v["n"] if v["n"] else None,
                      "mean_width_mw": v["width"] / v["n"] if v["n"] else None,
                      "interval_score": v["score"] / v["n"] if v["n"] else None,
                      "hours": v["n"]} for lv, v in per.items()} for m, per in scores.items()}
    return {"table": table, "alphas": alphas, "published": published}

           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE parameter = 'windspeed100' AND place = 'Raahe')     AS wind_raahe,
           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE parameter = 'windspeed100' AND place = 'Oulu')      AS wind_oulu,
           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE parameter = 'windspeed100' AND place = 'Helsinki')  AS wind_helsinki,

           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE parameter = 'windspeed100' AND place = 'Kalajoki')     AS farm_kalajoki,
           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE parameter = 'windspeed100' AND place = 'Lestijärvi')   AS farm_lestijarvi,
           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE parameter = 'windspeed100' AND place = 'Ii')           AS farm_ii,

    FROM weather_forecast

SELECT w.hour_start,

"""
weather_model.py
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Can a model built on public weather forecasts and the calendar beat
Fingrid's own day-ahead forecasts of wind output and consumption?

Inputs per hour (sql/analysis/26_weather_model_panel.sql), all known when
Fingrid issues its forecast for day D at 12:00 Finnish time on D-1:

  weather     temperatures and 100 m wind speeds forecast 48 h earlier at
              eight towns and seven wind-farm areas (Open-Meteo,
              src/openmeteo_forecast.py)
  calendar    Finnish hour and weekday, holidays, eves, bridge days, the
              Christmas period, July, the sun's elevation
              (src/finnish_calendar.py)
  history     consumption at the same hour a week earlier and the mean of
              day D-2; wind capacity as it stood at the end of D-2

Two gradient-boosted tree models per variable (scikit-learn
HistGradientBoostingRegressor):

  weather            the inputs above only
  weather_fingrid    Fingrid's forecast plus a learned correction: a
                     heavily regularised model of Fingrid's error on the
                     same inputs (and Fingrid's forecast itself). With
                     nothing to learn it returns Fingrid's forecast, so it
                     asks whether the weather and the calendar still know
                     something Fingrid's forecast missed.

The tree settings were fixed before the published backtest; six settings of
the correction model were tried on it, and none beat Fingrid by more than
2 % (the published one is the most regularised).

Wind is modelled as a capacity factor (output / capacity) so that a growing
fleet does not look like a windier year.

Backtest (rolling origin): the last BACKTEST_DAYS days with actuals are
forecast one at a time with a model refitted every REFIT_DAYS days on
everything known two days before the first day it forecasts. Scores are
mean absolute errors next to Fingrid's; the Diebold-Mariano test (daily
loss differences, Newey-West variance) says whether a difference is more
than luck.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from datetime import date, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

import finnish_calendar as cal

HELSINKI = ZoneInfo("Europe/Helsinki")
BACKTEST_DAYS = 182
REFIT_DAYS = 7
MIN_TRAIN_DAYS = 120
DM_LAGS = 7
MODELS = ("weather", "weather_fingrid")
WIND_PLACES = ("vaasa", "kokkola", "pori", "raahe", "oulu", "helsinki")
FARMS = ("kristinestad", "kalajoki", "lestijarvi", "ii", "tornio", "kyyjarvi", "pyhajoki")
PARAMS = {
    "weather": dict(max_iter=300, learning_rate=0.05, max_leaf_nodes=31, min_samples_leaf=40,
                    l2_regularization=1.0, early_stopping=False, random_state=0),
    "weather_fingrid": dict(max_iter=100, learning_rate=0.02, max_depth=3, min_samples_leaf=400,
                            l2_regularization=10.0, early_stopping=False, random_state=0),
}


def panel(rows: list[dict]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The SQL rows with Finnish calendar columns, known-history columns and the capacity factor."""
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df["hour_start"] = pd.to_datetime(df["hour_start"], utc=True)
    for c in df.columns:
        if c != "hour_start":
            df[c] = pd.to_numeric(df[c], errors="coerce").astype(float)
    local = df["hour_start"].dt.tz_convert(HELSINKI)
    df["day"] = local.dt.date
    df["hour_fi"] = local.dt.hour
    df["isodow"] = local.dt.dayofweek + 1
    days = {d: cal.day_features(d) for d in df["day"].unique()}
    for k in ("holiday", "holiday_eve", "bridge_day", "christmas_period", "july"):
        df[k] = df["day"].map(lambda d: days[d][k])
    df["sun_elevation"] = [cal.sun_elevation(t.to_pydatetime()) for t in df["hour_start"]]
    df["heating"] = np.maximum(15.0 - df["temp_c"], 0.0)
    df["temp_day_mean"] = df.groupby("day")["temp_c"].transform("mean")
    speeds = df[[f"wind_{p}" for p in WIND_PLACES]]
    df["wind_mean"] = speeds.mean(axis=1)
    df["wind_spread"] = speeds.std(axis=1)
    farms = df[[f"farm_{p}" for p in FARMS]]
    df["farm_mean"] = farms.mean(axis=1)
    df["farm_cube"] = (farms.clip(0, 13) ** 3).mean(axis=1)    # turbine output flattens above ~13 m/s

    # History that was known at issue time (noon of D-1): days up to D-2.
    by_day = df.groupby("day")
    daily_cons = by_day["consumption_mw"].mean()
    last_cap = by_day["wind_capacity_mw"].last().ffill()
    df["cons_d2_mean"] = df["day"].map(lambda d: daily_cons.get(d - timedelta(days=2), np.nan))
    df["cap_known"] = df["day"].map(lambda d: last_cap.get(d - timedelta(days=2), np.nan))
    week = df.set_index("hour_start")["consumption_mw"]
    df["cons_week_ago"] = df["hour_start"].map(lambda t: week.get(t - pd.Timedelta(days=7), np.nan))
    df["wind_cf"] = df["wind_mw"] / df["cap_known"]
    df["fingrid_wind_cf"] = df["fingrid_wind_mw"] / df["cap_known"]
    return df


CALENDAR = ["hour_fi", "isodow", "holiday", "holiday_eve", "bridge_day", "christmas_period", "july", "sun_elevation"]
FEATURES = {
    "consumption": CALENDAR + ["temp_c", "temp_helsinki", "temp_oulu", "heating", "temp_day_mean",
                               "wind_helsinki", "cons_d2_mean", "cons_week_ago"],
    "wind": ["hour_fi", "sun_elevation", "temp_vaasa", "wind_mean", "wind_spread", "farm_mean", "farm_cube"]
            + [f"wind_{p}" for p in WIND_PLACES] + [f"farm_{p}" for p in FARMS],
}
TARGET = {"consumption": "consumption_mw", "wind": "wind_cf"}
FINGRID = {"consumption": "fingrid_consumption_mw", "wind": "fingrid_wind_cf"}


def features(variable: str, model: str) -> list[str]:
    return FEATURES[variable] + ([FINGRID[variable]] if model == "weather_fingrid" else [])


def _to_mw(variable: str, df: pd.DataFrame, pred: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    if variable == "wind":
        return np.clip(pred, 0, None) * df["cap_known"].to_numpy()
    return pred


def fit_predict(df: pd.DataFrame, variable: str, model: str, train_until: date, target_days) -> pd.Series:
    """Fit on hours of days <= train_until with a known target; predict the hours of target_days (MW)."""
    from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingRegressor

    cols = features(variable, model)
    target, fingrid = TARGET[variable], FINGRID[variable]
    train = df[(df["day"] <= train_until) & df[target].notna() & df[fingrid].notna()]
    test = df[df["day"].isin(set(target_days)) & df[fingrid].notna()]
    if train["day"].nunique() < MIN_TRAIN_DAYS or test.empty:
        return pd.Series(dtype=float)
    if model == "weather_fingrid":            # learn Fingrid's error, add the correction to its forecast
        reg = HistGradientBoostingRegressor(**PARAMS[model]).fit(train[cols], train[target] - train[fingrid])
        pred = test[fingrid].to_numpy() + reg.predict(test[cols])
    else:
        pred = HistGradientBoostingRegressor(**PARAMS[model]).fit(train[cols], train[target]).predict(test[cols])
    return pd.Series(_to_mw(variable, test, pred), index=test.index)


def diebold_mariano(loss_a: np.ndarray, loss_b: np.ndarray, lags: int = DM_LAGS) -> dict:
    """DM test of equal mean loss on daily loss series; positive mean = b is better. Two-sided p-value."""
    d = np.asarray(loss_a) - np.asarray(loss_b)
    n = len(d)
    u = d - d.mean()
    var = u @ u / n
    for k in range(1, lags + 1):
        var += 2 * (1 - k / (lags + 1)) * (u[k:] @ u[:-k]) / n
    stat = d.mean() / math.sqrt(var / n) if var > 0 else 0.0
    p = math.erfc(abs(stat) / math.sqrt(2))
    return {"mean_difference": float(d.mean()), "statistic": float(stat), "p_value": float(p), "days": int(n)}


def backtest(df: pd.DataFrame, variable: str, days: int = BACKTEST_DAYS, refit: int = REFIT_DAYS) -> dict:
    """Rolling-origin replay of the last *days* days that have actuals and a Fingrid forecast."""
    target, fingrid_mw = (("consumption_mw", "fingrid_consumption_mw") if variable == "consumption"
                          else ("wind_mw", "fingrid_wind_mw"))
    known = df[df[target].notna() & df[fingrid_mw].notna() & df["cap_known"].notna()]
    complete = known.groupby("day").size()
    test_days = sorted(d for d, n in complete.items() if n >= 23)[-days:]
    preds = {m: pd.Series(dtype=float) for m in MODELS}
    for i in range(0, len(test_days), refit):
        block = test_days[i:i + refit]
        for m in MODELS:
            p = fit_predict(df, variable, m, block[0] - timedelta(days=2), block)
            preds[m] = pd.concat([preds[m], p])
    idx = preds[MODELS[0]].index
    for m in MODELS:
        idx = idx.intersection(preds[m].index)
    rows = df.loc[idx].copy()
    rows["actual"] = rows[target]
    rows["fingrid"] = rows[fingrid_mw]
    for m in MODELS:
        rows[m] = preds[m].loc[idx]
    errs = {k: (rows[k] - rows["actual"]).abs() for k in ("fingrid",) + MODELS}
    out = {"days": int(rows["day"].nunique()), "hours": int(len(rows)),
           "first_day": str(min(rows["day"])) if len(rows) else None,
           "last_day": str(max(rows["day"])) if len(rows) else None,
           "mae_mw": {k: float(e.mean()) for k, e in errs.items()},
           "rmse_mw": {k: float(np.sqrt(((rows[k] - rows["actual"]) ** 2).mean())) for k in errs},
           "bias_mw": {k: float((rows[k] - rows["actual"]).mean()) for k in errs}}
    out["skill_vs_fingrid"] = {m: 1 - out["mae_mw"][m] / out["mae_mw"]["fingrid"] for m in MODELS}
    daily = pd.DataFrame({k: e for k, e in errs.items()}).groupby(rows["day"]).mean()
    out["diebold_mariano"] = {m: diebold_mariano(daily["fingrid"].to_numpy(), daily[m].to_numpy()) for m in MODELS}
    month = pd.to_datetime(rows["day"]).dt.strftime("%Y-%m")
    by_month = pd.DataFrame({k: e for k, e in errs.items()}).groupby(month).mean()
    out["by_month"] = [{"month": mo, **{k: float(v) for k, v in r.items()}} for mo, r in by_month.iterrows()]
    out["rows"] = rows
    return out


def forecast_day(df: pd.DataFrame, variable: str, day: date) -> pd.DataFrame | None:
    """Both models' forecasts for every hour of *day*, trained on what was known two days before it."""
    fingrid_mw = "fingrid_consumption_mw" if variable == "consumption" else "fingrid_wind_mw"
    hours = df[(df["day"] == day) & df[fingrid_mw].notna() & df["cap_known"].notna()]
    if len(hours) < 23:
        return None
    out = hours[["hour_start", fingrid_mw]].rename(columns={fingrid_mw: "fingrid"}).copy()
    for m in MODELS:
        p = fit_predict(df, variable, m, day - timedelta(days=2), [day])
        if p.empty:
            return None
        out[m] = p
    return out


DAY_TYPES = ("holiday", "holiday_eve", "bridge_day", "christmas_period", "july")


def day_type(row) -> str:
    """The most specific calendar label of an hour, in DAY_TYPES order, else weekend / weekday."""
    for k in DAY_TYPES:
        if row[k] == 1:
            return k
    return "weekend" if row["isodow"] >= 6 else "weekday"


def errors_by_day_type(df: pd.DataFrame) -> list[dict]:
    """Fingrid's day-ahead consumption error by kind of day, over every hour with both values."""
    known = df[df["consumption_mw"].notna() & df["fingrid_consumption_mw"].notna()].copy()
    known["err"] = known["fingrid_consumption_mw"] - known["consumption_mw"]
    known["kind"] = known.apply(day_type, axis=1)
    out = []
    for kind in ("weekday", "weekend") + DAY_TYPES:
        part = known[known["kind"] == kind]
        if len(part):
            out.append({"kind": kind, "days": int(part["day"].nunique()), "hours": int(len(part)),
                        "mae_mw": float(part["err"].abs().mean()), "bias_mw": float(part["err"].mean())})
    return out

-- =============================================================
-- 27_hydrology_state.sql
-- One row per day: how full the Finnish reservoirs are and how much
-- water is coming in, each against what is normal for that day of the
-- year. The state variables of src/hydro_flex.py.
--
--   storage_z     mean of the five reservoir/lake z-scores: (level -
--                 that calendar day's 2000-2022 median) / that day's
--                 standard deviation; 0 = a normal level for the date,
--                 +1 = one standard deviation fuller than normal
--   level_<name>_z   the five parts (Lokka, Porttipahta, Oulujärvi,
--                 Saimaa, Näsijärvi)
--   inflow_z      log of the unregulated Tornionjoki's discharge
--                 against that calendar day's 2000-2022 log mean and
--                 standard deviation
--   nve_filling   mean filling of the Norwegian reservoirs (NO1-NO5,
--                 weekly, carried forward to every day of the week)
--
-- Calendar days are matched as month-day, with 29 February folded
-- onto 28 February; each norm pools a +/- 7 day window around the
-- date, so a norm rests on about 15 x 23 values.
--
-- Parameters: start, end (date, end exclusive)
-- Techniques: window-pooled seasonal norms, LATERAL carry-forward
-- =============================================================

WITH doy AS (
    SELECT series, day, value,
           -- day of a 365-day year (29 Feb -> 28 Feb)
           EXTRACT(DOY FROM make_date(2001, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM day)::int,
                   LEAST(EXTRACT(DAY FROM day)::int, CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM day) = 2 THEN 28 ELSE 31 END)))::int AS d,
           CASE WHEN series = 'flow_tornionjoki' THEN ln(GREATEST(value, 1)) ELSE value END AS x
    FROM hydrology_daily
    WHERE series LIKE 'level_%%' OR series = 'flow_tornionjoki'
),
norm AS (                                      -- per series and day of year: 2000-2022 mean and sd, +/- 7 days
    SELECT n.series, n.d,
           AVG(h.x)         AS mean_x,
           STDDEV_SAMP(h.x) AS sd_x
    FROM (SELECT DISTINCT series, d FROM doy) n
    JOIN doy h
      ON h.series = n.series
     AND h.day < DATE '2023-01-01'
     AND LEAST(abs(h.d - n.d), 365 - abs(h.d - n.d)) <= 7
    GROUP BY n.series, n.d
),
z AS (
    SELECT h.series, h.day, (h.x - n.mean_x) / NULLIF(n.sd_x, 0) AS z
    FROM doy h JOIN norm n USING (series, d)
    WHERE h.day >= %(start)s AND h.day < %(end)s
),
days AS (
    SELECT day,
           AVG(z) FILTER (WHERE series LIKE 'level_%%')             AS storage_z,
           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE series LIKE 'level_%%')           AS levels,
           MAX(z) FILTER (WHERE series = 'level_lokka')            AS level_lokka_z,
           MAX(z) FILTER (WHERE series = 'level_porttipahta')      AS level_porttipahta_z,
           MAX(z) FILTER (WHERE series = 'level_oulujarvi')        AS level_oulujarvi_z,
           MAX(z) FILTER (WHERE series = 'level_saimaa')           AS level_saimaa_z,
           MAX(z) FILTER (WHERE series = 'level_nasijarvi')        AS level_nasijarvi_z,
           MAX(z) FILTER (WHERE series = 'flow_tornionjoki')       AS inflow_z
    FROM z
    GROUP BY day
)
SELECT d.day, d.storage_z, d.levels, d.level_lokka_z, d.level_porttipahta_z, d.level_oulujarvi_z,
       d.level_saimaa_z, d.level_nasijarvi_z, d.inflow_z, nve.nve_filling
FROM days d
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (                            -- the latest Norwegian week on or before the day
    SELECT AVG(value) AS nve_filling
    FROM hydrology_daily
    WHERE series LIKE 'nve_no%%'
      AND day = (SELECT max(day) FROM hydrology_daily WHERE series = 'nve_no1' AND day <= d.day)
) nve ON true
ORDER BY d.day;

"""
hydro_flex.py
~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Does Finnish hydropower make more room for wind when its reservoirs are full?

The wind chapter (src/wind_allocation.py) finds that only about a tenth of an
extra MW of wind is absorbed by Finnish hydro. Hydro plants can only hold water
back if there is room to store it and they must release it if too much is coming
in, so the share should depend on the state of the water. This module lets it:

    part = b_wind * wind + b_ws * wind * storage + b_wi * wind * inflow
           + storage + inflow + nuclear + heating degrees
           + hour-of-day, weekday, month and year fixed effects

on the hourly balance panel (sql/analysis/24) joined with the water state of the
day before (sql/analysis/27: reservoir levels and the unregulated Tornionjoki's
discharge, each against its 2000-2022 norm for the date). The day before is used
because today's levels are partly the result of today's hydro decisions.

The share of +1 MW of wind that a part absorbs at storage s (inflow at its mean)
is -(b_wind + b_ws * s); its 95 % interval comes from the Newey-West covariance
of the two coefficients. As a check that does not assume a straight line, the
plain wind regression is also fitted separately in the driest, middle and
fullest third of days.

Associations, not proven causes: the water state also moves with things the
model does not see (Swedish hydro, prices).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import numpy as np

import wind_allocation as wa

PARTS = ("hydro_mw", "net_import_mw", "other_mw", "consumption_mw")
STATES = ("storage_z", "inflow_z")
Z95 = wa.Z95
HELSINKI = ZoneInfo("Europe/Helsinki")


def _as_date(d):
    return date.fromisoformat(d[:10]) if isinstance(d, str) else d


def join_state(panel_rows: list[dict], state_rows: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    """Each hour gets the water state of the previous Finnish day (and its Finnish year);
    hours without a complete state are dropped."""
    state = {_as_date(r["day"]): r for r in state_rows}
    out = []
    for r in panel_rows:
        t = r["hour_start"]
        t = datetime.fromisoformat(t.replace("Z", "+00:00")) if isinstance(t, str) else t
        local = t.astimezone(HELSINKI)
        s = state.get(local.date() - timedelta(days=1))
        if s is None or s["storage_z"] is None or s["inflow_z"] is None:
            continue
        out.append({**r, "year_fi": local.year, "storage_z": float(s["storage_z"]), "inflow_z": float(s["inflow_z"])})
    return out


def design(rows: list[dict]) -> tuple[np.ndarray, list[str]]:
    X, names = wa.design(rows)
    wind = X[:, names.index("wind_mw")]
    cols, extra = [], []
    for k in STATES:
        v = np.array([r[k] for r in rows], dtype=float)
        cols += [v, wind * v]
        extra += [k, f"wind_x_{k}"]
    years = np.array([r["year_fi"] for r in rows])
    for y in sorted(set(years.tolist()))[1:]:
        cols.append((years == y).astype(float))
        extra.append(f"year_{y}")
    return np.column_stack([X] + cols), names + extra


def fit(rows: list[dict], parts=PARTS) -> dict:
    """Coefficients and HAC covariances of wind and its interactions for every part."""
    X, names = design(rows)
    iw, iws, iwi = (names.index(n) for n in ("wind_mw", "wind_x_storage_z", "wind_x_inflow_z"))
    out = {"hours": len(rows), "parts": {}}
    for part in parts:
        y = np.array([r[part] for r in rows], dtype=float)
        keep = ~np.isnan(y) & ~np.isnan(X).any(axis=1)
        Xk, yk = X[keep], y[keep]
        beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(Xk, yk, rcond=None)
        V = wa.newey_west(Xk, yk - Xk @ beta)
        idx = [iw, iws, iwi]
        out["parts"][part] = {"beta": beta[idx].tolist(), "cov": V[np.ix_(idx, idx)].tolist(), "hours": int(keep.sum())}
    return out


def share_at(fitted: dict, part: str, storage: float, inflow: float = 0.0) -> dict:
    """Share of +1 MW of wind absorbed by *part* (pushed out; for consumption: added) at a water state."""
    p = fitted["parts"][part]
    g = np.array([1.0, storage, inflow])
    sign = 1.0 if part == "consumption_mw" else -1.0
    est = sign * float(g @ np.array(p["beta"]))
    se = float(np.sqrt(g @ np.array(p["cov"]) @ g))
    return {"share": est, "ci_low": est - Z95 * se, "ci_high": est + Z95 * se}


def interaction(fitted: dict, part: str, which: str = "storage_z") -> dict:
    """How much the share moves per standard deviation of the state, with its 95 % interval and p-value."""
    import math

    p = fitted["parts"][part]
    i = 1 if which == "storage_z" else 2
    sign = 1.0 if part == "consumption_mw" else -1.0
    b, se = sign * p["beta"][i], math.sqrt(p["cov"][i][i])
    return {"per_sd": b, "ci_low": b - Z95 * se, "ci_high": b + Z95 * se,
            "p_value": math.erfc(abs(b / se) / math.sqrt(2)) if se > 0 else 1.0}


def by_tercile(rows: list[dict], key: str = "storage_z") -> list[dict]:
    """The plain wind regression (src/wind_allocation.py) in each third of days by *key*."""
    vals = np.array([r[key] for r in rows])
    cuts = np.quantile(vals, [1 / 3, 2 / 3])
    out = []
    for i, (lo, hi) in enumerate(((-np.inf, cuts[0]), (cuts[0], cuts[1]), (cuts[1], np.inf))):
        part = [r for r, v in zip(rows, vals) if lo < v <= hi]
        f = wa.fit(part, PARTS)
        out.append({"tercile": i + 1, "hours": f["hours"], "state_mean": float(np.mean([r[key] for r in part])),
                    "shares": {k: (1.0 if k == "consumption_mw" else -1.0) * f["responses"][k]["wind_mw"]["coef"]
                               for k in PARTS},
                    "hydro_ci": sorted((-f["responses"]["hydro_mw"]["wind_mw"]["ci_high"],
                                        -f["responses"]["hydro_mw"]["wind_mw"]["ci_low"]))})
    return out

-- 28_consumption_hourly.sql
-- One row per UTC hour: Finland's consumption and the measured
-- temperature, the input of the counterfactual "what would Finland
-- have used without the strike?" (src/strike_effect.py).
--
--   consumption_mw   dataset 124, all 4 quarters of the hour
--   temp_c           mean of Helsinki, Jyväskylä, Oulu, Rovaniemi
--                    (178, 182, 196, 185), each with >= 16 of its
--                    20 three-minute readings
--   day_fi, hour_fi  Finnish calendar day and hour
--
-- Measured (not forecast) temperatures: this looks back at events
-- that are over, so the weather that happened is the right control.
--
-- Parameters: start, end (timestamptz, end exclusive)
-- Techniques: FILTER pivot, HAVING completeness rules, AT TIME ZONE
-- =============================================================

WITH hourly AS (
    SELECT dataset_id,
           date_trunc('hour', start_time) AS hour_start,
           AVG(value)                     AS value
    FROM fingrid_observation
    WHERE dataset_id IN (124, 178, 182, 196, 185)
      AND start_time >= %(start)s AND start_time < %(end)s
    GROUP BY dataset_id, hour_start
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= CASE WHEN dataset_id = 124 THEN 4 ELSE 16 END
),
wide AS (
    SELECT hour_start,
           MAX(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id = 124)                     AS consumption_mw,
           AVG(value) FILTER (WHERE dataset_id IN (178, 182, 196, 185))   AS temp_c,
           COUNT(*)   FILTER (WHERE dataset_id IN (178, 182, 196, 185))   AS cities
    FROM hourly
    GROUP BY hour_start
)
SELECT hour_start,
       (hour_start AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki')::date                  AS day_fi,
       EXTRACT(HOUR FROM hour_start AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Helsinki')::int  AS hour_fi,
       consumption_mw,
       temp_c
FROM wide
WHERE consumption_mw IS NOT NULL AND cities = 4
ORDER BY hour_start;

"""
strike_effect.py
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
How much electricity did Finland not use during the 2024 political strikes?
And does consumption that the weather cannot explain follow industrial output?

Event study with a counterfactual. A gradient-boosted model learns hourly
consumption (sql/analysis/28) from what the strikes did not change: measured
temperature (now, and its 24 h and 72 h means), the Finnish calendar (hour,
weekday, holidays, eves, bridge days, the Christmas period, July, the sun's
elevation, the time of year) and a slow time trend. It is trained on every
hour outside the strike periods (and BUFFER_DAYS around them), then asked what
the strike days would have used. The effect is what was used minus that.

Is the effect more than the model's ordinary error? A placebo test: the same
procedure, refitted each time, on N_PLACEBO periods of the same length and
starting weekday in the heating season of other years and months, with no
strike. The p-value is the share of placebo effects at least as large (in
absolute size) as the strike's; the 90 % band is their 5th-95th percentile.

Monthly link to industry. A second model without the time trend (weather and
calendar only) leaves, month by month, the consumption the weather and the
calendar do not explain; it is set against Statistics Finland's seasonally
adjusted volume index of manufacturing output (StatFin 14mh). Both drift upward
over these years, and two drifting series correlate whether or not they are
linked, so trend_check() also correlates their month-to-month changes and fits
the index with a linear trend beside it: only a link that survives those counts.

The model only measures a gap; that the strike caused it rests on the timing
and on the placebo test, not on proof. Strikes also hit transport and services,
so the effect is the whole economy's, not industry's alone.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from datetime import date, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

import finnish_calendar as cal

HELSINKI = ZoneInfo("Europe/Helsinki")
BUFFER_DAYS = 3
N_PLACEBO = 40
SEED = 0
PARAMS = dict(max_iter=300, learning_rate=0.05, max_leaf_nodes=31, min_samples_leaf=40,
              l2_regularization=1.0, early_stopping=False, random_state=0)

EVENTS = [
    {"key": "industry_feb", "name": "Industrial Union stoppage", "start": date(2024, 2, 1), "end": date(2024, 2, 2),
     "what": "two-day stoppage across Finnish industry, about 60,000 workers",
     "source": "https://www.teollisuusliitto.fi/en/2024/01/extensive-political-strike/"},
    {"key": "political_feb", "name": "Wide political strikes", "start": date(2024, 2, 12), "end": date(2024, 2, 16),
     "what": "coordinated strikes across sectors, power plants on 14-16 February",
     "source": "https://www.jhl.fi/en/news/jhls-political-strike-is-expanding-around-finland-dramatic-decrease-in-commuter-traffic-train-traffic-will-stop-power-plants-will-be-shut-down-three-day-strike-within-early-childhood-educ/"},
    {"key": "ports_mar_apr", "name": "Ports and transport strike", "start": date(2024, 3, 11), "end": date(2024, 4, 7),
     "what": "ports and rail stopped; paper and pulp mills shut for lack of transport",
     "source": "https://www.sak.fi/?p=31419"},
]

TREND_FEATURES = ["hour_fi", "isodow", "holiday", "holiday_eve", "bridge_day", "christmas_period", "july",
                  "sun_elevation", "doy_sin", "doy_cos", "temp_c", "heating", "temp_24h", "temp_72h", "days"]
NO_TREND_FEATURES = [f for f in TREND_FEATURES if f != "days"]


def panel(rows: list[dict]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df["hour_start"] = pd.to_datetime(df["hour_start"], utc=True)
    df["day_fi"] = pd.to_datetime(df["day_fi"]).dt.date
    for c in ("consumption_mw", "temp_c"):
        df[c] = pd.to_numeric(df[c]).astype(float)
    df = df.sort_values("hour_start").reset_index(drop=True)
    local = df["hour_start"].dt.tz_convert(HELSINKI)
    df["isodow"] = local.dt.dayofweek + 1
    days = {d: cal.day_features(d) for d in df["day_fi"].unique()}
    for k in ("holiday", "holiday_eve", "bridge_day", "christmas_period", "july"):
        df[k] = df["day_fi"].map(lambda d: days[d][k])
    df["sun_elevation"] = [cal.sun_elevation(t.to_pydatetime()) for t in df["hour_start"]]
    doy = local.dt.dayofyear
    df["doy_sin"], df["doy_cos"] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * doy / 365.25), np.cos(2 * np.pi * doy / 365.25)
    df["heating"] = np.maximum(15.0 - df["temp_c"], 0.0)
    temp = df.set_index("hour_start")["temp_c"]
    df["temp_24h"] = temp.rolling("24h").mean().to_numpy()
    df["temp_72h"] = temp.rolling("72h").mean().to_numpy()
    df["days"] = (df["hour_start"] - df["hour_start"].min()).dt.total_seconds() / 86400
    return df


def _mask(df: pd.DataFrame, ranges, buffer: int = 0) -> np.ndarray:
    m = np.zeros(len(df), bool)
    for start, end in ranges:
        m |= ((df["day_fi"] >= start - timedelta(days=buffer)) & (df["day_fi"] <= end + timedelta(days=buffer))).to_numpy()
    return m


def fit_predict(df: pd.DataFrame, train: np.ndarray, features=TREND_FEATURES) -> np.ndarray:
    from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingRegressor

    reg = HistGradientBoostingRegressor(**PARAMS).fit(df.loc[train, features], df.loc[train, "consumption_mw"])
    return reg.predict(df[features])


def gap(df: pd.DataFrame, start: date, end: date, exclude) -> dict:
    """Actual minus counterfactual over [start, end], with the model trained outside *exclude* (+ buffer)."""
    pred = fit_predict(df, ~_mask(df, exclude, BUFFER_DAYS))
    period = _mask(df, [(start, end)])
    diff = df.loc[period, "consumption_mw"].to_numpy() - pred[period]
    return {"mean_mw": float(diff.mean()), "gwh": float(diff.sum() / 1000), "hours": int(period.sum()),
            "share": float(diff.sum() / pred[period].sum()), "pred": pred, "period": period}


def placebo_starts(df: pd.DataFrame, event: dict, n: int = N_PLACEBO, seed: int = SEED) -> list[date]:
    """Starts of placebo periods: same length and starting weekday, October-April, data complete,
    clear of every event and its buffer."""
    length = (event["end"] - event["start"]).days
    blocked = _mask(df, [(e["start"], e["end"]) for e in EVENTS], BUFFER_DAYS + length + 1)
    have = df.groupby("day_fi").size()
    full = {d for d, k in have.items() if k >= 23}
    candidates = sorted({d for d, b in zip(df["day_fi"], blocked)
                         if not b and d.month in (10, 11, 12, 1, 2, 3, 4) and d.weekday() == event["start"].weekday()
                         and all(d + timedelta(days=i) in full for i in range(length + 1))})
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    return sorted(rng.choice(candidates, size=min(n, len(candidates)), replace=False).tolist())


def event_study(df: pd.DataFrame, event: dict, n_placebo: int = N_PLACEBO) -> dict:
    events = [(e["start"], e["end"]) for e in EVENTS]
    res = gap(df, event["start"], event["end"], events)
    period = res.pop("period")
    pred = res.pop("pred")
    days = (df.loc[period, ["day_fi", "consumption_mw"]].assign(pred=pred[period])
            .groupby("day_fi").agg(actual=("consumption_mw", "mean"), counterfactual=("pred", "mean")))
    length = (event["end"] - event["start"]).days
    placebos = []
    for s in placebo_starts(df, event, n_placebo):
        p = gap(df, s, s + timedelta(days=length), events + [(s, s + timedelta(days=length))])
        placebos.append(p["mean_mw"])
    placebos = np.array(placebos)
    return {**res, "daily": [{"day": str(d), "actual_mw": float(r.actual), "counterfactual_mw": float(r.counterfactual)}
                             for d, r in days.iterrows()],
            "placebo_n": len(placebos),
            "placebo_band_mw": [float(np.percentile(placebos, 5)), float(np.percentile(placebos, 95))] if len(placebos) else None,
            "placebo_p": float((np.abs(placebos) >= abs(res["mean_mw"])).mean()) if len(placebos) else None}


def monthly_residual(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Mean consumption the weather and calendar do not explain, per month (MW), from a model without trend."""
    pred = fit_predict(df, np.ones(len(df), bool), NO_TREND_FEATURES)
    month = pd.to_datetime(df["day_fi"]).dt.strftime("%Y-%m")
    out = pd.DataFrame({"month": month, "resid": df["consumption_mw"] - pred, "n": 1})
    return out.groupby("month").agg(resid_mw=("resid", "mean"), hours=("n", "sum")).reset_index()


def trend_check(x, y) -> dict:
    """Does y follow x beyond a shared trend? Correlation of levels, of month-to-month changes,
    and the slope of x in y ~ 1 + t + x with its t-statistic (plain OLS: few points)."""
    x, y = np.asarray(x, float), np.asarray(y, float)
    t = np.arange(len(x), dtype=float)
    X = np.column_stack([np.ones_like(t), t, x])
    beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None)
    resid = y - X @ beta
    se = math.sqrt(resid @ resid / (len(x) - 3) * np.linalg.inv(X.T @ X)[2, 2])
    return {"r_levels": float(np.corrcoef(x, y)[0, 1]), "r_changes": float(np.corrcoef(np.diff(x), np.diff(y))[0, 1]),
            "slope_with_trend": float(beta[2]), "slope_se": float(se), "slope_t": float(beta[2] / se), "n": len(x)}
